nodes.title: SG-7.7 · Worker startup recovery for unfinished executions and stale locks
nodes.body:
Context: backend/worker/internal has config, lock, logging, report, runner and store packages but no recovery. store.Store persists executions as JSON; runner.Run takes a lock file via lock.Acquire, which leaves the file behind if the process dies. Desired behavior: a new recovery package scans for unfinished executions (PENDING, RUNNING, RECOVERING) and resumes each, or marks it RECOVERING when resuming fails, and removes a stale lock file. Expected result: the worker can start after a crash without manual cleanup. Why: the product requires recovery after process restart and never assuming the worker ran continuously.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given PENDING, RUNNING and RECOVERING executions in the store, When Recover runs, Then each is passed to the Resumer exactly once
- Given COMPLETED, FAILED or AWAITING_APPROVAL executions, When Recover runs, Then they are neither resumed nor modified
- Given the Resumer returns an error for an execution, When Recover runs, Then that execution is saved as RECOVERING with the error text, UpdatedAt set from the injected clock, and the remaining executions are still processed
- Given a lock file older than StaleAfter by the injected clock, When startup recovery runs, Then the lock file is removed before executions are resumed
- Given a lock file younger than StaleAfter or no lock file, When startup recovery runs, Then no lock is removed and no error is returned


## Scope
- In scope: New package backend/worker/internal/recovery
- In scope: New RECOVERING status constant in backend/worker/internal/store/store.go
- Out of scope: Wiring into a worker main or cmd entry point (none exists)
- Out of scope: Changing runner.Run, lock.Acquire or the config file schema
- Out of scope: Real process-liveness detection
- Preserve: store.Store JSON format and atomic Save
- Preserve: lock.Acquire semantics
- Preserve: Existing runner and store tests


## Technical constraints
- Go 1.22 module github.com/worldseed/storyforge/worker
- No database or external dependencies
- All dependencies injected for unit tests: store, resumer, clock, lock filesystem


## Definition of done
- All acceptance criteria are met by product code
- go build ./... passes in backend/worker


## Non-functional requirements
- Recovery must not hold the lock file while resuming, since runner.Run acquires it


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Recover scans the store and resumes unfinished executions
nodes.body:
Context: store.Store.List returns all executions sorted by ID. Desired behavior: Recoverer.Recover resumes every unfinished execution through an injected Resumer and skips finished or approval-pending ones. Expected result: a Result lists resumed IDs. Why: unfinished work continues after a restart.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given PENDING, RUNNING and RECOVERING executions, When Recover runs, Then Resumer.Resume is called once for each in ID order
- Given COMPLETED, FAILED and AWAITING_APPROVAL executions, When Recover runs, Then Resume is not called for them and the store is not written
- Given store.List returns an error, When Recover runs, Then Recover returns an error wrapping it and resumes nothing


## Scope
- In scope: Recoverer, Resumer and ExecutionStore types
- In scope: Recover method
- Out of scope: Lock handling
- Out of scope: Marking failed resumes
- Preserve: store package API


## Technical constraints
- ExecutionStore interface must be satisfied by *store.Store


## Definition of done
- Recover implemented and compiles


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · A failed resume marks the execution RECOVERING with the error
nodes.body:
Context: the Round lifecycle defines a RECOVERING state but store has no such status. Desired behavior: add store.StatusRecovering and have Recover persist it with the error text and clock time when Resume fails, then continue with the next execution. Expected result: Result lists marked IDs. Why: failures must be visible, not silently dropped.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given Resume returns an error for one execution, When Recover runs, Then the store receives that execution with Status RECOVERING, Error equal to the error text and UpdatedAt equal to the injected clock
- Given the first of two executions fails to resume, When Recover runs, Then the second is still resumed
- Given Save of the RECOVERING record fails, When Recover runs, Then Recover returns an error wrapping it


## Scope
- In scope: store.StatusRecovering constant
- In scope: Marking logic in Recover
- Out of scope: Admin API changes
- Preserve: Existing Status constants and values


## Technical constraints
- StatusRecovering value is the string RECOVERING


## Definition of done
- Constant added and used by Recover


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Startup releases a stale lock file before recovery
nodes.body:
Context: lock.Acquire writes a PID file that a crashed process never removes, blocking runner.Run with ErrLocked. Desired behavior: Startup inspects the lock file modification time through an injected LockFS and removes it when now minus modtime exceeds StaleAfter. Expected result: Startup returns whether a lock was released together with the Recover result. Why: a crash must not block the worker forever.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a lock modtime older than StaleAfter, When Startup runs, Then LockFS.Remove is called with LockPath and Result.LockReleased is true
- Given a lock modtime younger than StaleAfter, When Startup runs, Then Remove is not called and LockReleased is false
- Given the lock file does not exist, When Startup runs, Then no error is returned and Recover still runs
- Given Remove fails, When Startup runs, Then Startup returns an error wrapping it and does not resume executions


## Scope
- In scope: LockFS interface and OS implementation
- In scope: ReleaseStaleLock and Startup methods
- Out of scope: PID liveness checks
- Out of scope: Editing the lock package
- Preserve: lock.Lock format


## Technical constraints
- Clock injected via func() time.Time
- StaleAfter must exceed Timeout times attempts; documented in code comment


## Dependencies
- Recoverer type from the scan requirement (same package)


## Definition of done
- Startup implemented and compiles


## Clarifying questions
- None

steps.symbol: new: ExecutionStore, Resumer, Config, Result, Recoverer, New
steps.action: Create package recovery with interface ExecutionStore {List() ([]store.Execution, error); Save(store.Execution) error}, interface Resumer {Resume(ctx context.Context, e store.Execution) error}, struct Config {LockPath string; StaleAfter time.Duration}, struct Result {Resumed []string; Marked []string; LockReleased bool}, struct Recoverer holding st, resumer, lockFS LockFS, now func() time.Time, cfg Config, and constructor New(cfg Config, st ExecutionStore, r Resumer, lfs LockFS, now func() time.Time) *Recoverer.
steps.code: func New(cfg Config, st ExecutionStore, r Resumer, lfs LockFS, now func() time.Time) *Recoverer { return &Recoverer{cfg: cfg, st: st, resumer: r, lockFS: lfs, now: now} }
steps.expected: Package declares the types; compiles together with the lock-file Act.

steps.action: Implement Recover(ctx) (Result, error): call st.List, wrap error as fmt.Errorf("recovery: list: %w", err). For each execution whose Status is store.StatusPending, StatusRunning or StatusRecovering call resumer.Resume; on nil append ID to Result.Resumed; on error set e.Status=store.StatusRecovering, e.Error=err.Error(), e.UpdatedAt=r.now(), call st.Save (return fmt.Errorf("recovery: save %s: %w") on failure, with the result so far), append ID to Result.Marked and continue. Skip all other statuses.
steps.code: switch e.Status { case store.StatusPending, store.StatusRunning, store.StatusRecovering: default: continue }
steps.expected: Recover returns Resumed and Marked IDs in ID order.

nodes.title: Act: Implement stale lock release and Startup
nodes.body:
Create backend/worker/internal/recovery/locks.go with the LockFS abstraction, an os implementation, ReleaseStaleLock and Startup, which releases a stale lock then runs Recover. Uses Recoverer fields from recovery.go.

## Acceptance criteria
- A lock older than StaleAfter is removed
- Startup runs Recover only after the lock check succeeds


## Scope
- In scope: locks.go
- Out of scope: lock package changes
- Preserve: lock.Acquire


## Technical constraints
- Recoverer and Result come from recovery.go in the same package
- New file: `backend/worker/internal/recovery/locks.go`


## Dependencies
- recovery.go


## Definition of done
- Package builds


## Clarifying questions
- None
nodes.summary: Add LockFS, ReleaseStaleLock and Startup to the recovery package.
nodes.description: Create backend/worker/internal/recovery/locks.go with the LockFS abstraction, an os implementation, ReleaseStaleLock and Startup, which releases a stale lock then runs Recover. Uses Recoverer fields from recovery.go.
acceptance_criteria: A lock older than StaleAfter is removed
Startup runs Recover only after the lock check succeeds
technical_constraints: Recoverer and Result come from recovery.go in the same package

steps.action: Define interface LockFS {ModTime(path string) (time.Time, error); Remove(path string) error} and struct OSLockFS implementing it with os.Stat(path).ModTime() and os.Remove(path).
steps.code: func (OSLockFS) ModTime(p string) (time.Time, error) { fi, err := os.Stat(p); if err != nil { return time.Time{}, err }; return fi.ModTime(), nil }

steps.action: Implement ReleaseStaleLock() (bool, error): call lockFS.ModTime(cfg.LockPath); if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) return false,nil; other errors wrapped as "recovery: stat lock: %w"; if now().Sub(mod) <= cfg.StaleAfter return false,nil; otherwise call lockFS.Remove, wrapping errors as "recovery: remove lock: %w" and ignoring fs.ErrNotExist, and return true,nil. Add a comment that StaleAfter must exceed Timeout times (MaxRetries+1).
steps.expected: Returns true only when a stale lock was removed.

steps.action: Implement Startup(ctx) (Result, error): call ReleaseStaleLock; on error return Result{} and the error; then call Recover and set Result.LockReleased to the released value before returning.
steps.expected: Stale lock is released before any execution is resumed.
